coverage.main: Read all ten pages of the CVF open-access CVPR 2020 paper (pp. 1161-1170), including Sections 1-6, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-4 and references. Visually checked rendered PDF pp. 6-8 (Table 1, Section 5.1 setup, Table 2, Section 5.2, Table 3, Figure 4).
coverage.supplement: The CVF landing page links only the main PDF; no supplementary material, appendix or arXiv version was located. The paper itself does not reference a supplement. Nothing further is claimed inspected.
coverage.excluded_results: Table 1/2 diagonal cells and the Inception V4 column of Table 3 are white-box (source = target) and are excluded from transfer judgments. The Random Noise row is a non-transfer baseline retained as setup evidence. Figures 1-3 are qualitative attention/visual examples.

result_groups.locator: Table 1 off-diagonal ResNet V2/Inception V3/Inception V4/Inception-ResNet V2 columns (p. 6); Table 3 same targets except source Inception V4 (p. 8); Figure 4 undefended curves (p. 8); Sections 5.1-5.2, 5.4
result_groups.population: All 1,000 NeurIPS 2017 competition test images; adversarial samples generated on the source and fed to each target
result_groups.outcome: target top-1 accuracy (complement is unconditional misclassification)
result_groups.evidence: Section 5.1 defines the 1,000-image test set and top-1 accuracy metric. Table 1's No Perturbation row reports target accuracy below 100% on the same table (e.g., ResNet V2 89.6%), so target-clean-incorrect inputs are in the evaluated population. Section 5.2 states the resultant samples are directly fed to the source and other models; source white-box accuracies above zero (e.g., ResNet V2 FGSM 14.6%) show source failures are retained in the target accuracy denominator. Table 3 TAP values equal Table 1's Inception V4 row, consistent with one population.

result_groups.locator: Table 1 Ensemble column (p. 6); Table 3 Ensemble column (p. 8); Figure 4 Ensemble curve; Section 5.1 (p. 6)
result_groups.population: Same 1,000 images; target is the probability average of all four undefended models, including the source
result_groups.evidence: No Perturbation ensemble accuracy 99.8% shows clean-incorrect inputs are retained; same Section 5.2 feeding protocol. Because the ensemble contains the source model, it is not a disjoint black-box target and is kept separate from single-model transfer.

result_groups.locator: Table 2 (p. 7); Table 3 Adv-Inc-v3/Adv-IncRes-v2/Ens3/Ens4 columns (p. 8); Figure 4 defended curves (p. 8); Sections 5.1-5.2
result_groups.population: Same 1,000 images and undefended sources; targets are four public adversarially trained models
result_groups.evidence: The Section 5.2 feeding protocol and accuracy metric are shared, retaining source failures. No clean accuracy is reported for these four targets and no filtering statement is made, so target-clean-incorrect handling is not explicit for this group; not inferred from the undefended table.

f1.locator: Table 1 No Perturbation row (p. 6); Table 2 (p. 7); Table 3 (p. 8)
f1.evidence: Clean accuracy is reported separately for all four undefended source/target models and the ensemble on the 1,000-image test set. No clean accuracy is located for Adv-Inc-v3, Adv-IncRes-v2, Ens3-Adv-Inc-v3 or Ens4-Adv-Inc-v3. Missing entries are not an explicit pooled-only report, so unclear rather than no.

f2.evidence: Undefended and ensemble groups explicitly retain target-clean-incorrect inputs (clean rows below 100% in the same accuracy table); the defended group has no clean baseline or statement. Paper-level unclear by unanimity rule; any_explicit_yes = false.

f3.evidence: All transfer groups use target accuracy over every sample produced on the source, which is directly fed to all models; source white-box accuracies above zero show failures are present. This is an explicit unconditioned-transfer design choice, not missing reporting and not a claim the paper is wrong.

f4.evidence: No literal counts. With the stated 1,000-image set and no filtering, one-decimal percentages map to unique integers k/1,000 (e.g., 89.6% -> 896). However the Table 1 Inception V3 BIM white-box cell prints 0.01%, which is not k/1,000, so the denominator or displayed value is not uniformly consistent; Figure 4 gives graphical values only. Unique reconstruction therefore does not cover every surveyed result. This is recorded as a reporting inconsistency, not an error claim.

f5.evidence: Section 3 adopts the L-infinity norm; p. 7 fixes epsilon to 16 for all methods; C&W uses an L-infinity-constrained variant, random noise uses the same norm constraint, TI/TAP combinations keep clip_{x,epsilon}, and Figure 4 keeps other parameters fixed. Pixel scale is not stated; 16 is consistent with 0-255 pixels but that scale is an inference, not reported.

f6.evidence: Footnotes link public third-party pretrained target/source checkpoints (Cadene pretrained-models.pytorch; TensorFlow adv_imagenet_models). No ATA code, adversarial samples or per-example outputs are linked, and a bounded GitHub search located none. Public model weights alone do not supply the attack implementation or outputs; this is not a claim that no release exists.

bounds_checks.locator: Table 1 No Perturbation row and off-diagonal cells (p. 6); Table 3 undefended columns (p. 8)
bounds_checks.reason: Same fixed targets, same 1,000-image population and denominator, unconditional misclassification (100 - accuracy), no source-success conditioning. A second extraction from the rendered p. 6 image (same non-blind auditor, not a separate person) reproduced all 72 single-target and 24 ensemble historical CSV values and nominal bounds exactly, and matched the PDF text layer. Table 3 adds nine eligible single-target cells not in the historical CSV (Inception V4 source; nominal / rounding-aware lower bounds in percentage points): TAP+ATA ResNet V2 36.0/35.90, Inception V3 73.7/73.60, Inception-ResNet V2 80.2/79.65; TI 32.5/32.40, 65.5/65.40, 73.1/72.55; TI+ATA 33.4/33.30, 71.5/71.40, 75.8/75.25. Table 3's TAP row duplicates Table 1. Figure 4 is graphical and not extracted. All rates are correlated within one paper.

bounds_checks.locator: Table 1 and Table 3 Ensemble columns; Section 5.1 (p. 6)
bounds_checks.reason: The identity holds for the fixed ensemble predictor on the same population, but the ensemble includes the source model, so these 24 historical plus three Table 3 cells (TAP+ATA 51.7/51.60, TI 41.5/41.40, TI+ATA 49.7/49.60) are not disjoint cross-model transfer. The historical 96-bound summary mixes them with single-target transfer; report separately.
No clean accuracy for the defended targets on this population; full-ImageNet or third-party accuracies must not be substituted. Excluded from bounds.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit; supersedes the partial rank-38 ledger note. The visual re-extraction is not independent verification by a different person.

The historical analytic_bounds.csv and summary are unchanged: 72 of its 96 rows are single-target transfer and 24 use an ensemble containing the source. Nine additional Table 3 single-target cells are recorded here only, pending the corpus-wide bounds assessment.
The 0.01% white-box cell does not affect the bounds (diagonal), but limits uniform count reconstruction. No runtime recomputation attempted.
